findings.message: The resolver step declares `env` twice. GitHub Actions rejects duplicate mapping keys during workflow validation, preventing both automatic and manual runs. Remove the duplicate block.

This is a second `else` in the same conditional, after the fallback beginning at line 41. Once the heredoc indentation is corrected, `bash -n` reports an unexpected `else`. Every invocation fails before resolving a run ID; replace the obsolete fallback rather than appending another branch.

Both resolver heredocs retain two leading spaces after YAML removes the run block's indentation. Bash cannot recognize their `PY` terminators and reports an unexpected end of file. The Python bodies also raise `IndentationError` if only the terminators are fixed. Unindent both Python bodies and their terminators to the run block's left margin.

The fallback still filters workflow runs to `pre-update-release`, repeating the branch-metadata mistake described in this change. The weekly workflow checks out that branch internally, but scheduled runs belong to the default branch. Consequently, neither fallback query finds scheduled scans; manual dispatch without a run ID fails or selects an older manually dispatched scan. Resolve runs using their actual workflow branch. See GitHub's [schedule semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#schedule) and [branch filter](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs#list-workflow-runs-for-a-workflow).

Checking `github.actor` skips the guard when a maintainer pushes a correction to a Dependabot PR. That synchronization run belongs to the maintainer, so the latest commit receives a skipped security check instead of being scanned. This particularly affects manual corrections to underfixed updates. Identify Dependabot PRs through `github.event.pull_request.user.login`; [github.actor identifies the workflow initiator](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#github-context).
